tasks.short: Read CVs in Recruitee against the vacancy and job order, and sort who fits.

today.trigger: New application lands in Recruitee or a manager opens a vacancy or job order.
steps: Open the vacancy and the manager's intake notes
Read each CV and motivation letter in Recruitee
Check hard requirements: driving licence C/CE, code 95, forklift, VCA, shift availability, Dutch or English level
Tag and move the candidate to a pipeline stage
Note doubts for a phone screen
drudgery: Reading many near-identical warehouse CVs in peak season
Checking certificates and licences by hand
Re-reading the intake notes for each candidate
today.time_sinks: Volume peaks before Q4 and summer, when warehouse vacancies get hundreds of applications and the same hard criteria are checked by eye.

lenses.faster: Hard criteria (licence, certificates, shifts, location) are checked by rules on a structured screening form; an LLM summarises each CV against the job profile so the recruiter reads one paragraph instead of the full CV.
lenses.autonomous: Each new application triggers the knock-out check and a fit summary written back to Recruitee as a note; no reminder needed.
lenses.ambitious: Every applicant gets a fair, documented read within 24 hours, and near-misses are tagged for other open roles across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses scanning 200 CVs for a code 95 card; what is left is talking to the borderline and interesting candidates.
lenses.options: For each candidate the tool shows fit for this vacancy plus two other open roles they might suit.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter owns the screening criteria and the summary prompt, and samples outcomes monthly for errors and bias.
reach: HR Administrator: certificate and right-to-work checks before contract
Hiring managers' first CV pass

tasks.human_edge: Judging non-standard careers, motivation and potential that a criteria check misses, and deciding who gets rejected.
tasks.pattern_why: Knock-out criteria are deterministic; the CV-to-profile summary is unstructured-to-structured and checkable; rejection stays with the recruiter because this is high-risk AI under the EU AI Act.

steps: Pull CV, answers to screening questions and vacancy profile via the Recruitee API
Run rule-based knock-out checks on structured answers
LLM writes a fit summary with evidence quotes per requirement
Write note and suggested tag back to Recruitee
Recruiter confirms stage move or rejection
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter decides every rejection and stage move; no automated rejection.
systems: LLM service under a DPA in the EU
data_needed: Job profiles with must-have and nice-to-have criteria
Historic hires and 90-day outcomes for calibration
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee candidate notes plus a screening log (input, summary, decision) kept for the AI Act and AVG audit trail.

evidence.claim: LLMs can summarise a CV against a job profile reliably enough for a human to verify.
AI used to screen or filter job applications is classified high-risk under the EU AI Act Annex III.
evidence.source: EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689), Annex III point 4

evidence.claim: An automated CV screener trained on past hires learned gender bias and was dropped.
evidence.source: Amazon recruiting tool, reported by Reuters 2018

risks: Bias against non-Dutch names, gaps or non-standard careers
Over-trust in the summary so CVs are no longer read
AVG: candidate data sent to a model without DPA or information notice
Works council consent needed (WOR art. 27) for a system that assesses applicants
research_questions: How many applications per warehouse vacancy in peak, and what share fail hard criteria?
Does Recruitee's API allow writing notes and tags back without a custom integration licence?
Does the summary agree with two recruiters' independent reads on a sample of 100 past CVs?
Will the OR agree to this under art. 27 WOR, and on what conditions?

tasks.short: Explain the job, shifts, pay scale, CAO terms and site conditions to candidates by phone and mail.

today.trigger: Candidate passes first screen, asks a question, or reaches the offer stage.
steps: Look up the CAO scale, shift pattern and allowances for the role
Call or mail the candidate with the details
Answer follow-up questions on travel, overtime, holidays, pension
Repeat at offer stage with exact numbers
drudgery: Answering the same questions about shift allowances and travel costs
Looking up the right CAO for transport versus warehouse
Writing the same explanation mails
today.time_sinks: Repeated questions per candidate and finding the right CAO table for each site and role.

lenses.faster: A role fact sheet per vacancy (scale, allowances, shifts, site, travel) is generated from SharePoint and AFAS once, and mail drafts pull from it.
lenses.autonomous: A candidate Q&A assistant on the careers page and WhatsApp answers standard questions from approved sources and hands off anything personal.
lenses.ambitious: Every candidate gets a clear net-pay example and a realistic job preview video per site, so fewer drop out in week one.
lenses.joy: No more retyping the shift allowance table; the recruiter spends the calls on doubts and selling the job.
lenses.options: Draft explanations in Dutch, English and Polish, and in a short and a detailed version.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter curates the approved answer base and reviews unanswered questions weekly.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: first-line pay and benefits questions
HR Administrator: pre-boarding information

tasks.human_edge: Reading a candidate's hesitation, negotiating, and being honest about hard parts of night shifts and peak weeks.
tasks.pattern_why: Answers come from a fixed, approved source set and are checkable; personal or salary-negotiation questions go to the recruiter.

in_practice.trigger: Candidate moves to the screening or offer stage, or sends a question.
steps: Retrieve vacancy fact sheet and CAO passages
Draft answer or information mail in the candidate's language
Flag questions outside the source set
Recruiter approves and sends from Recruitee
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter approves any mail with pay figures; the bot never makes offers or promises.
systems: Microsoft 365 Copilot or an Azure OpenAI chatbot
data_needed: Current CAO tables per site and role
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee candidate timeline; unanswered questions to a SharePoint list.

evidence.claim: Conversational assistants answer candidate FAQs and schedule interviews for high-volume hourly hiring.
Copilot in Outlook drafts mails grounded in SharePoint documents.

risks: Wrong pay or allowance figure creates an expectation with legal weight
Outdated CAO after indexation
Candidates feel processed rather than welcomed
research_questions: Which ten questions make up most candidate contacts?
How often do CAO tables change and who owns updating them?
Does a realistic job preview cut week-one drop-out at one site in a pilot?

tasks.short: Choose the best candidates and recommend them to the hiring manager.

today.trigger: Interviews and screens for a vacancy are done.
steps: Collect interview feedback in Recruitee
Compare candidates on notes and gut feel
Write a short recommendation to the manager
Discuss in a Teams call and agree on the choice
drudgery: Chasing managers for scorecards
Rewriting scattered notes into one comparison
today.time_sinks: Waiting for and assembling feedback, and writing comparisons from free-text notes.

lenses.faster: Feedback forms are structured per criterion and an LLM drafts a side-by-side shortlist with evidence from notes.
lenses.autonomous: When the last scorecard is in, the comparison draft appears; missing scorecards get an automatic reminder.
lenses.ambitious: Recommendations are checked against 90-day retention data, so the team learns which signals predict a hire who stays.
lenses.joy: Less copy-paste of notes, more real discussion with managers about who fits the team.
lenses.options: Show two or three hiring scenarios (best now, best potential, internal mover) with risks of each.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter designs the scorecards and reviews whether recommendations predicted 90-day success.
reach: HR Business Partner: workforce fit and internal mobility advice
People Analytics: quality-of-hire analysis

tasks.human_edge: Weighing team fit, manager preferences and fairness, and owning the recommendation.
tasks.pattern_why: The decision has legal and human weight; AI prepares the comparison, the recruiter and manager decide.

in_practice.trigger: All scheduled interviews for a vacancy have feedback in Recruitee.
steps: Pull structured scorecards and notes
Draft comparison table with evidence per criterion
Recruiter edits and adds judgment
Send to manager and decide together
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter writes the final recommendation; manager makes the decision.

evidence.claim: LLMs can summarise interview notes into a criterion comparison.
Structured interviews predict job performance better than unstructured ones.

risks: Draft frames the decision and anchors the manager
Notes contain biased language that gets amplified
AI Act high-risk obligations if the tool ranks candidates
research_questions: What share of managers fill in scorecards today?
Do recommendations differ in 90-day retention by manager or site?
Do managers prefer a ranked list or an unranked comparison?

tasks.short: Tell candidates where they stand: invites, holds, rejections, next steps.

today.trigger: Candidate moves stage, waits too long, or asks for an update.
steps: Check status in Recruitee
Pick and adapt a mail template
Call candidates who reached interview
Answer reply mails
drudgery: Personalising rejection mails
Chasing managers to know what to tell candidates
Candidates left waiting and calling in
today.time_sinks: Candidates stuck in a stage with no news, causing calls and mails, and writing personal rejections after interviews.

lenses.faster: Stage changes send templated mails automatically; post-interview rejections get an LLM draft using the interview feedback.
lenses.autonomous: A rule flags any candidate without contact for 5 working days and sends a status update or nudges the manager.
lenses.ambitious: Every candidate, including rejected ones, gets a timely, specific reply, which matters in a tight labour market where rejected drivers reapply.
lenses.joy: No more sending the hundredth standard mail; calls are kept for finalists and bad news after interviews.
lenses.options: Draft a warm, short and an extended-feedback version of a rejection to choose from.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter sets the communication SLAs and templates and watches candidate experience scores.
reach: Hiring managers' candidate follow-up
HR Administrator: pre-boarding mails after offer

tasks.human_edge: Delivering bad news to finalists and internal candidates by phone, and keeping relationships for future roles.
tasks.pattern_why: Most updates follow stage changes and timers; only personal post-interview feedback needs an LLM draft.

in_practice.trigger: Stage change in Recruitee or 5 working days without contact.
steps: Recruitee automation sends stage templates
Timer rule flags stale candidates
LLM drafts personal feedback for interviewed candidates
Recruiter approves personal mails; calls finalists
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter approves post-interview rejections; early-stage templates run without approval.

evidence.claim: ATSs send automated emails on pipeline stage changes.
evidence.source: Recruitee automated actions (model knowledge, verify current feature set)

evidence.claim: LLMs draft personalised rejection mails from notes.

risks: Wrong mail to wrong candidate on a mis-moved stage
Feedback reveals discriminatory reasoning in notes
AVG retention: rejected candidate data kept beyond 4 weeks without consent
research_questions: How long do candidates wait per stage today?
How many inbound status calls per week?
Does Recruitee support time-based triggers natively or is Power Automate needed?

tasks.short: Search for candidates on job boards, LinkedIn, referrals, agencies and job fairs.

today.trigger: Hard-to-fill vacancy (drivers, technicians, team leads) or too few applicants after a week.
steps: Write boolean searches on LinkedIn and job board CV databases
Review profiles and send outreach messages
Ask staff for referrals and check flex workers from agencies
Attend job fairs and regional events
Log prospects in Recruitee
drudgery: Tweaking search strings
Writing outreach one by one
Copying profiles into Recruitee
today.time_sinks: Manual search and outreach with low reply rates, and overlooking good flex workers already on site.

lenses.faster: AI-assisted search turns the job profile into searches and drafts personalised outreach for review.
lenses.autonomous: Agency hours data flags flex workers with long tenure and good attendance as candidates for permanent roles when a matching vacancy opens.
lenses.ambitious: A standing talent pool of former applicants, alumni and flex workers is re-engaged before every vacancy, reducing agency fees.
lenses.joy: Less copy-paste, more time at job fairs and with team leads who know good people.
lenses.options: Five outreach variants and three channel mixes per vacancy, tested on reply rate.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter runs a sourcing playbook per role family and tracks which channel yields hires who stay 90 days.
reach: HR Business Partner: flex-to-permanent conversion plans
Finance: agency spend reduction via conversions

tasks.human_edge: Building relationships with candidates, schools, agencies and team leads, and the personal pitch.
tasks.pattern_why: Sourcing needs judgment and personal contact; AI speeds search and drafting while the recruiter chooses whom to approach.

in_practice.trigger: Vacancy open longer than 10 days or flagged hard-to-fill.
steps: Generate search strings and target lists from the job profile
Match flex workers from agency hours exports
Draft outreach messages
Recruiter reviews and sends
Log prospects in Recruitee
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter picks targets and sends every message.
data_needed: Agency hours and attendance per flex worker
in_practice.logs_to: Recruitee sourced candidates and a channel report in Power BI.

evidence.claim: LinkedIn Recruiter offers AI-assisted search and message drafting.
Flex worker attendance data can identify conversion candidates.

risks: AVG: re-contacting past applicants without consent
Agency contracts may charge a conversion fee or forbid poaching
Generic AI outreach lowers reply rates
research_questions: What do the three agency contracts say about converting flex workers?
Which channel produced the hires still there after 90 days last year?
How many past applicants gave consent for a talent pool?

tasks.short: Check whether our selection criteria and tests are fair, relevant and legal, and propose changes.

today.trigger: Yearly review, complaint, high early turnover, or a new role profile.
steps: Export pipeline data from Recruitee to Excel
Compare pass rates by stage and group where data allows
Review job profiles and requirements for necessity
Write recommendations for the HR Director
drudgery: Cleaning exports
Matching hires to 90-day outcomes in AFAS by hand
today.time_sinks: Joining Recruitee and AFAS data, and lacking data on protected characteristics.

lenses.faster: A Power BI funnel joins Recruitee stages with AFAS 90-day outcomes so the analysis is ready instead of built each time.
lenses.autonomous: Monthly report flags criteria with high rejection rates and low link to 90-day retention.
lenses.ambitious: Every requirement is validated against job performance, and the AI Act documentation for any screening tool is kept current.
lenses.joy: No more spreadsheet joins; time goes to the conversation about which requirements really matter.
lenses.options: Scenarios showing how many more applicants pass if a requirement (e.g. Dutch level B1) is relaxed.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter owns the selection standard and the AI governance file for recruitment tools.
reach: People Analytics: recruitment funnel models
HR Director: compliance with College voor de Rechten van de Mens guidance

tasks.human_edge: Judging what is fair and necessary, and arguing changes with managers and the works council.
tasks.pattern_why: Data prep is automatable, but conclusions on fairness and legality need a human owner.

steps: Nightly join of Recruitee and AFAS data
Dashboard of pass rates and 90-day outcomes per criterion
LLM drafts findings and options
Recruiter and People Analytics review
Proposal to HR Director and OR
in_practice.human_gate: HR Director approves changes to criteria.

evidence.claim: Dutch human rights institute has published guidance against recruitment discrimination including by algorithms.
evidence.source: model knowledge (College voor de Rechten van de Mens)

evidence.claim: Deployers of high-risk AI must monitor and keep logs.

risks: No lawful data on ethnicity, so fairness can only be tested indirectly
Small numbers per vacancy make statistics unreliable
Findings misread as proof of no bias
research_questions: Are rejection reasons recorded consistently in Recruitee?
Which requirements show no link to 90-day retention?
Can the AFAS extract join to Recruitee on a stable key?

tasks.short: Plan how and where we recruit for coming demand, including peak season and new sites.

today.trigger: Budget cycle, peak season planning, new customer contract, or high turnover at a site.
steps: Collect headcount plans from site managers
Review time-to-hire, turnover and agency use
Choose channels, employer branding and budget
Agree plan with HR Director and sites
drudgery: Collecting plans in different Excel formats
Rebuilding the same numbers each season
today.time_sinks: Gathering demand from sites and reconciling it with turnover and agency data.

lenses.faster: A standard demand template feeds a model combining turnover, absence and order forecasts into a hiring forecast per site.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly forecast refresh flags sites where hiring is behind plan.
lenses.ambitious: A rolling 12-month workforce plan per site with a deliberate mix of permanent, flex and conversions.
lenses.joy: Less number gathering, more time on employer brand and partnerships with ROC schools.
lenses.options: Three scenarios: low, expected, and high volume, with cost of agency vs permanent hiring.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter designs the planning model and assumptions and reviews them quarterly.
reach: FP&A Analyst: personnel cost forecasts
HR Business Partner: strategic workforce planning

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating priorities with site managers and reading local labour markets.
tasks.pattern_why: Strategy depends on judgment and negotiation; AI helps with data and scenarios.

in_practice.trigger: Quarterly planning and before peak season.
steps: Pull turnover, absence and agency hours
Build scenario forecast
Draft channel and budget plan
Review with site managers and HR Director
in_practice.human_gate: HR Director signs off the plan and budget.

evidence.claim: Scenario models from historical turnover and volume data are standard spreadsheet/BI work that LLMs help build.

risks: Forecasts trusted without checking customer contract assumptions
Sites ignore the plan
research_questions: How accurate were last year's peak hiring estimates?
What is the full cost of a flex worker vs permanent hire per role?
Can operations share volume forecasts monthly?

tasks.short: Set up and run applicant tests such as forklift practicals, language and planner skills tests.

today.trigger: Vacancy needs a test (planner, team lead, technician, forklift driver).
steps: Pick or update the test
Schedule the test with candidate and site
Have the site run practical tests
Collect and score results
Feed scores into the selection
drudgery: Scheduling with sites
Scoring paper or Excel tests
Keeping tests up to date
today.time_sinks: Scheduling practical tests and scoring by hand.

lenses.faster: LLM drafts job-related test items from the job profile; online tests auto-score; self-scheduling links handle bookings.
lenses.autonomous: Moving a candidate to the test stage sends an online test or a booking link for the practical.
lenses.ambitious: Every test is validated against 90-day performance and offered in several languages.
lenses.joy: No more scoring piles of paper tests; time goes on designing good work samples.
lenses.options: Several parallel test versions to limit item leakage.
lenses.altitude: The recruiter owns the test catalogue and checks validity and adverse impact yearly.
reach: Learning and Development: link test results to onboarding training
Site team leads: practical assessment standard

tasks.human_edge: Observing practical skills and safety behaviour, and judging fairness of test content.
tasks.pattern_why: Scheduling, delivery and scoring are multi-step with tool calls; test design and use of results need human approval.

in_practice.trigger: Candidate moved to test stage in Recruitee.
steps: Send online test or booking link
Auto-score and write result to Recruitee
Flag outliers
Recruiter reviews results before decision
in_practice.human_gate: Recruiter approves test content and reviews every score before use.

evidence.claim: Online skills test platforms with auto-scoring integrate with ATSs.
LLMs can draft job-related test items for expert review.

risks: Tests that disadvantage non-native speakers without job reason
Unvalidated AI-written items
Works council consent needed for testing
research_questions: Which tests predict 90-day success today?
Do language tests reject candidates who later do well as flex workers?
Does the OR need to approve new tests?

role.altitude: From screening, mailing and scheduling to owning the hiring system: screening criteria, templates, sourcing playbooks, tests and the AI governance file, measured on hires still productive at day 90.
reach: HR Administrator: pre-boarding and certificate checks
Compensation and Benefits: first-line pay questions from candidates
People Analytics: funnel and quality-of-hire reporting
HR Business Partner: flex-to-permanent conversion and workforce planning
FP&A: agency spend and hiring cost forecasts
role.ceiling_note: Roughly 35-45% of recruiter hours can be freed, mostly in screening, status mails and candidate questions. The limits are the EU AI Act high-risk rules for recruitment AI, works council consent, AVG, and the parts that need personal contact: interviews, finalist calls, negotiations and relationships with site managers and agencies.
skills_to_grow: Writing and testing screening criteria and prompts
Basic funnel analytics in Power BI
AI Act and AVG compliance for recruitment tools
role.ambitious_version: Two recruiters run an always-on hiring engine for three sites: every applicant answered within a day, a talent pool of past applicants and flex workers ready before peak, and each criterion and channel checked against 90-day retention, cutting agency spend and lifting the North Star.
